Each hour: time, direction and speed (knots, g = gust), odds of 12kt or more, regime, waves, tide height in ft with r rising or f falling. OUTFLOW NOT RIDDEN = Squamish outflow, never recommend. OFF DIR = direction does not work at that spot.
Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Thu, Oct 29 7:22am to 6:29pm; Fri, Oct 30 7:23am to 6:28pm; Sat, Oct 31 7:25am to 6:26pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Thu, Oct 29 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Easterly morning, and the North Shore is blowing harder than the page. At 6am Point Atkinson read E 23, up from 16 at 5am. The English Bay buoy had ENE 16 gusting 18 and Sand Heads E 17. Halibut Bank was ENE 18 gusting 25 at 5am.

My pick is Boundary Bay from about 8am to 2pm, E 14 to 16. The tide stays above 11ft all day (high 14.4ft at 9:40am, low 11.6ft at 2:34pm), so plenty of water. If Sand Heads still reads 15+ from the east at 8am, go.

Erwin could surprise at first light. The page only has 8 to 9 gusting 15, but if Point Atkinson still reads 20+ at 7am, it's worth a look. Expect it gusty, easing by about 11am.

Porteau is a maybe early. Pam Rocks read N 23 at 5am and 19 at 6am, and Pemberton is 3 hPa above Vancouver, right on the forecast. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north at 8am, go. The flood to 15.9ft at 9:40am may flatten the swell.
